chapter: Chicago in the 1920s: Bix, Armstrong, Morton
title: Other records: Roy Palmer, Biscuit Eater and Tiny Parham's last session
summary: He cannot recall titles; he remembers Biscuit Eater and discovers years later that he played on Tiny Parham's Frogtown Blues.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well did you make a lot of records at that time?
I made quite a few with all of them. We went up into Richmond, Indiana. Jeanette. Yeah. And I made them with Roy Palmer. Don't ask me the names of them because I can't.
Did you make records with Roy Palmer? Oh heck yeah.
One I remember was a biscuit eater. I remember that.
Turkish. Wait a minute. You know what a biscuit is? Yes.
Now you got it. Thank you.
What is this? You like a leucutian teacher or something? No.

That's the only one I can remember and the reason I can remember is because it was brought to my attention. You see the reason I don't remember titles. I was, I had to be one of the last ones to make a record with Tiny Parm. Uh huh. What do you know about, or maybe you don't. Like a little ending would make Dipper Mount. I mean King Oliver made Dipper Mount. We don't know what the title of that thing is. See they make part of the introduction and we hear it and when they knock off we go ahead and play. You know in them days? Uh huh. We got a record date. While we put up our instruments, he's in there giving the names. Name them.

Petita hit anything you know. So this particular session, it was drums, guitar, organ and playing it. Tiny Parm dies three months later. Never did hear the record. So I had AAF station in Chicago and they played this record and I said I recognized my own, he said I don't recognize the organ. So I called him and asked him, I said is that a Decker record, Tiny Parm you just finished playing? He said yes. I said what was the name of it? He said Frogtown Blues. You know? That's the first I knew what it was.
